CHOOSE BY WHAT GLASS DOES

Three priorities.
Find your glass.

Start with the performance you need. These groups are not mutually exclusive, and glass choices can be combined in one window.

01 / EXPLORELight & privacy ↓For daylight, glare & privacy 02 / EXPLOREThermal comfort ↓For heat transfer & insulation 03 / EXPLORESafety & protection ↓For impact & breakage behaviour

01 / FOR DAYLIGHT, GLARE & PRIVACY

Light & privacy

Choose how much you see through the glass, how much light enters and how much glare you want to soften.

01 / DAYLIGHT & VIEWS

Clear float glass

Clear, flat glass that lets in daylight and preserves the view.

Consider for General glazing where suitable, or as a base for processed glass.

Ordinary annealed float is not safety glass. Appearance alone does not tell you performance.Explore clear glass ↗
02 / GLARE CONTROL

Tinted glass

Colour in the glass can reduce glare and incoming solar heat.

Consider for Bright, glare-prone windows where less daylight is acceptable.

Tint is not insulation, a safety treatment or guaranteed privacy; thermal-stress assessment may be needed.Understand tinted glass ↗
03 / PRIVACY

Frosted / obscure glass

A finish, pattern or translucent interlayer softens views while admitting light.

Consider for Privacy-focused windows, such as bathrooms, and partitions.

Privacy levels vary. Safety requirements still need to be specified separately.Explore privacy glass ↗

02 / FOR HEAT TRANSFER & INSULATION

Thermal comfort

Explore coatings and sealed glazing units for thermal comfort. Compare the whole window, not just the glass.

04 / COATING

Low-E glass

A coating that reduces heat transfer through the glass.

Consider for Thermal comfort in living spaces and bedrooms.

Choose for your climate. Low-E does not automatically mean double glazing.Understand Low-E ↗
05 / INSULATED UNIT

Double glazing

Two panes with a sealed cavity between them to improve insulation.

Consider for Windows where thermal performance is a priority.

Glass, cavity and frame all matter. Double glazing alone is not a safety-glass specification.Explore double glazing ↗

03 / FOR IMPACT & BREAKAGE BEHAVIOUR

Safety & protection

Understand how glass responds to impact and what happens if it breaks. The right treatment depends on the application.

06 / SAFETY TREATMENT

Toughened glass

Heat-treated glass that breaks into small fragments rather than large shards.

Consider for Correctly specified windows, doors and shower screens.

It is not unbreakable and does not hold fragments in place after breakage.Understand toughened glass ↗
07 / BONDED GLASS

Laminated glass

An interlayer bonds glass sheets and helps retain broken fragments.

Consider for Suitable windows and doors where fragment retention matters.

Acoustic and security versions need their own specification; laminated glass alone does not guarantee fall protection.Explore laminated glass ↗

COMBINE & CUSTOMISE

One window.
Several choices.

A window can combine Low-E, double glazing and toughened or laminated glass. Ask a qualified glazier or designer to confirm the right specification for your project.

Custom is an option across all groups. Ask about sizes, tint, finish and glass combinations, subject to supplier confirmation. Environmental claims need product-specific evidence; a thermal feature alone is not proof of sustainability.

Read the complete glass guide ↗

General education, not a product specification or confirmation of available stock. Manufacturer references and limitations are in our glass guide.

FROM REQUEST TO DELIVERY

From your brief.
To your front door.

GLASS QUALITY. CLEAR COSTS.A human-led journey, with the specification, responsibilities and delivery scope agreed before you order.

  1. 01
    YOU → FABINT

    Send your brief

    Tell us your window sizes, glass requirements, quantity, delivery location and target date. A drawing or photo helps.

  2. 02
    FABINT → YOU

    Compare your window quote

    We aim to return your window quote within seven days, with glass specifications, costs in AUD and a local benchmark where available.

  3. 03
    YOUR APPROVAL

    Approve the details

    Choose an option and agree the final specification, price, payment terms, delivery scope and lead time in writing.

  4. 04
    AFTER APPROVAL

    Make and check

    The supplier prepares your order. Quality evidence and any agreed inspection are reviewed before dispatch.

  5. 05
    SUPPLIER → CARRIER

    Arrange shipping

    Imported orders follow the agreed freight and customs arrangements; local orders travel within Australia. Confirm GST, duty and delivery inclusions.

  6. 06
    CARRIER → YOU

    Delivered to your door

    Delivery follows the agreed destination and access arrangements. Check your goods on arrival and report any damage promptly.

GOOD TO KNOW

Typical order journey, subject to agreed supplier terms. Seven days is our quote target, not a delivery promise. Installation and independent inspection are included only when explicitly quoted.

Submitting a request is not placing an order. Our pilot is personally managed; we do not take online payments.
